pull.title: fix(providers): a custom provider's models must appear the moment it is added
pull.body:
## What was wrong

Adding a custom provider on the **Providers** tab produced a card that reported its models while nothing else in the process had them. `GET /v1/models`, the **Models** page, the **Model Config** pickers and `~/.fcc/codex-model-catalog.json` were all empty for that provider. The only recovery was a restart — or, by accident, a second registry mutation.

Measured on the reporting install's `~/.fcc/logs/server.log` (all +03:00):

| Time | Event |
| --- | --- |
| 01:14:06 | last process restart |
| 03:05:32 | `POST /admin/api/custom-providers` — provider created |
| 03:05:37–39 | the create's hot reload sweeps **all** providers' `/models` |
| **03:05:39.883** | `Provider model discovery skipped: provider=custom_b_ai reason=query failure: PermissionDeniedError` |
| 03:06:09 | `PATCH /admin/api/custom-providers/custom_b_ai` — a second mutation |
| **03:06:14.360** | `Provider model discovery cached: provider=custom_b_ai models=44` |

There is no `Starting Claude Code Proxy...` line after 01:14:06, so the restart the report credited the fix to never happened. The PATCH did it.

## Mechanism

The create route called two things that each went to the upstream:

1. `ProviderRuntimeManager.replace()` fires a fire-and-forget sweep of **every** provider's `/models` (`provider_manager.py:459-461`).
2. The route then awaited `test_provider`, which fetches `/models` again (`admin_custom_routes.py:227` → `application.py:275-299`).

So a host registered one second earlier was asked for its model list **twice, concurrently, with the same brand-new key**. One of the two came back `PermissionDeniedError`. That failure was only logged (`discovery.py:155-160` — no caller and no UI learned of it), and the response's `models` array came from the **test result**, not from the catalogue (`admin_custom_routes.py:226-234`) — so the card could truthfully advertise 44 models the catalogue did not hold. On top of that, `test_provider` cached un-enriched infos while discovery cached models.dev-enriched ones, and `updateCustomProviderCard` never rewrote the model-count line.

## Fix

- **One fetch per create.** `ProviderRuntimeManager.replace()` takes `background_refresh`; a registry mutation names the one provider it changed and gets the new `refresh_provider_models()` instead — one awaited, provider-scoped discovery, with **one bounded retry** for the provider that just changed (a gateway that has not finished propagating a key answers 403 once and then serves the list fine). No periodic timer was added.
- **A discovery failure is reported.** `ProviderDiscoveryFailure` carries `error_type` and a redacted message back through `ProviderModelRefreshResult`. Create / enable / add-key / remove-key responses carry a `discovery` block (`{provider_id, ok, model_count, error_type, message}`), and the card renders it red with the upstream's reason instead of settling into a healthy-looking card.
- **The response reports the catalogue.** `model_count` and `models` come from the cache the discovery just filled, not from an independent probe.
- **One cache-and-publish seam.** `cache_enriched_model_infos()` in `providers/runtime/discovery.py` is now the only place model infos are enriched from models.dev and cached — used by both background discovery and the admin refresh button, so the catalogue no longer depends on which one filled it.
- **UI.** The custom card's "Test" button reads **"Refresh models"**, matching the identical `POST /admin/api/providers/{id}/test` call on a static remote card ("Test connection" stays for `kind === "local"`), and `updateCustomProviderCard` now rewrites the model-count line in place.
- **Docs.** New `docs/USAGE.md` "Custom providers" section, a `README.md` paragraph, an `ARCHITECTURE.md` "Custom Providers" subsection, and a paragraph in the in-dashboard Guide. `docs/AGENT_SPEC_CUSTOM_PROVIDERS.md` ("Temporary spec; delete before release") is deleted, its still-true parts folded into `ARCHITECTURE.md`.

Version bumped 6.21.0 → **6.22.0** (MINOR: new response field + changed UI behaviour), `uv lock` in the same commit.

## Verification

### Lint and types

```
$ uv run ruff format --check
1005 files already formatted
$ uv run ruff check
All checks passed!
$ uv run ty check
All checks passed!
```

### Tests

```
$ uv run pytest tests/api tests/contracts -q --tb=line
2 failed, 1466 passed, 5 skipped

$ uv run pytest tests/application tests/cli tests/config tests/core tests/runtime \
      tests/regression tests/test_brand_contract.py tests/test_model_overrides.py -q --tb=line
1 failed, 3974 passed, 1 skipped

$ uv run pytest tests/providers tests/messaging tests/scripts tests/websearch -q --tb=line
12 failed, 2649 passed, 32 skipped
```

**Baseline note:** the 15 failures are exactly the known pre-existing local baseline on unmodified `main` — 8 websearch tests that read the real `~/.fcc/.env`, 6 PowerShell installer tests, and `tests/runtime/test_provider_manager.py::test_catalog_publication_tracks_warm_refresh_and_direct_cache`. No new failures.

jsdom: `tests/api/test_admin_static_jsdom.py` — **159 passed** (157 existing + 2 new).

New tests:

```
tests/api/test_admin_custom_providers.py::test_create_publishes_models_to_the_catalogue_not_only_the_card
tests/api/test_admin_custom_providers.py::test_create_fetches_the_new_provider_models_exactly_once
tests/api/test_admin_custom_providers.py::test_create_reports_discovery_failure_in_the_response
tests/api/test_admin_custom_providers.py::test_create_retries_the_mutated_provider_once
tests/api/test_admin_custom_providers.py::test_enable_toggle_publishes_models_without_a_restart
tests/api/test_admin_custom_providers.py::test_add_key_republishes_the_catalogue
tests/api/test_model_catalog.py::test_custom_provider_models_appear_in_v1_models_after_create
tests/api/test_model_catalog.py::test_custom_provider_model_admin_block_reports_the_catalogue_count
tests/providers/test_custom_providers.py::test_test_provider_caches_models_dev_enriched_infos
tests/providers/test_custom_providers.py::test_discovery_failure_for_one_provider_does_not_evict_others
tests/runtime/test_provider_manager.py::test_replace_only_refreshes_the_mutated_provider_when_scoped
tests/runtime/test_provider_manager.py::test_scoped_refresh_retries_once_then_reports_the_failure
tests/api/test_admin_static_jsdom.py::test_custom_provider_card_labels_its_refresh_and_updates_the_count
tests/api/test_admin_static_jsdom.py::test_a_create_with_a_failed_discovery_does_not_render_a_healthy_card
```

The route-level tests run the real registry, the real hot reload, the real discovery, the real model cache and the real `/v1/models` — only the upstream HTTP client is doubled. The previous double stubbed the runtime, which is precisely where the defect lived.

### Browser drive

A scratch MCC on port **8199** with `HOME`/`USERPROFILE` redirected to a throwaway directory (never the user's `~/.fcc`, never their server on 8082), against a local FastAPI stub on 8196 serving 44 `{id,object,created,owned_by}` rows including `glm-5.3-flash`, with a 403 mode. Ports checked free with `netstat -ano` first.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Stub `/models` hits during one create | **1** (was 2) |
| Card after create, no reload | `CONFIGURED` · `1 key · failover · 44 models` |
| Card button label | **Refresh models** (static local cards still say "Test connection") |
| `GET /admin/api/custom-providers` | `model_count: 44` |
| `GET /v1/models` | 88 custom rows = both prefixed variants × 44, incl. `anthropic/custom_stub_ai/glm-5.3-flash` and `claude-3-freecc-no-thinking/custom_stub_ai/glm-5.3-flash` |
| `GET /admin/api/model-admin` | `custom_stub_ai` block, `model_count: 44` |
| Models page **Hide all** | writes `custom_stub_ai/*`, `hidden_count: 44`; **Show all** restores `hidden_count: 0` |
| Model Config picker | 44 `custom_stub_ai/*` options; primary + a fallback chain entry saved and round-tripped to `MODEL=custom_stub_ai/glm-5.3-flash`, `MODEL_FALLBACKS=custom_stub_ai/stub-model-01` with no validation error |
| `codex-model-catalog.json` | 88 `custom_stub_ai` references, rewritten on every mutation |
| Add key (2nd key) | `2 keys · failover · 44 models`, **1** stub hit |
| Disable then enable | disable → `model_count 0`, **0** hits; enable → `model_count 44`, `discovery.ok true`, **1** hit, no restart |
| 403 create | `discovery.ok false`, `error_type PermissionDeniedError`, card pill `PERMISSIONDENIEDERROR`, meta `query failure: PermissionDeniedError`, `0 models`, warning banner naming Refresh models. **2** stub hits (the one bounded retry) |
| Recovery | stub back to 200 → **Refresh models** on the failed card takes it from `0 models` to `44 models` in place, no page reload |
| Console errors | **0** |

Screenshots: `screenshots-custom-providers/01-create-success-card.png`, `02-models-page-hide-all.png`, `03-model-config-picker.png`, `04-model-config-saved.png`, `05-discovery-failure-card.png`, `06-refresh-models-recovers-count.png`, `07-guide-custom-providers.png`.

## Residual risks

- **`AdminRuntimePort.reload_providers` changed signature** (added keyword-only `refresh_provider_id`, now returns `dict[str, Any]` instead of `None`). It is an internal Protocol with one production implementation; the test double in `tests/api/test_admin_custom_providers.py` was updated. Any out-of-tree implementation would break.
- **The bounded retry costs one extra upstream call on a genuine failure** (two `/models` requests instead of one when the host is really refusing). Retry delay is 0.25 s and the retry count is 2 attempts total, both hard-coded parameters rather than settings — deliberately, to avoid adding a knob for Part A.
- **`refresh_provider_models` holds `_replace_lock` across the retry**, so a mutation that fails discovery blocks another mutation for up to ~0.25 s plus two upstream round trips. `connected_provider_changed` already had the same shape.
- **A disabled or keyless entry is not probed** (`_discovery_target` returns `None`), so those mutations fall back to the old blanket background sweep. That is the pre-existing behaviour, not a new one.
- **The jsdom harness is close to its 180 s subprocess timeout** under a fully parallel run and errored twice on this machine at ~99 % CPU; it passes cleanly when the file is run on its own (159 passed) and each harness invocation takes ~40 s standalone. This is the known 99 %-hang flake, not a new regression — my additions cost ~0.75 s per run.
- **Part B is untouched.** Custom providers still have no models.dev bucket (so limits and reasoning efforts come from the cross-provider vote), no per-key health readout, no onboarding credit, and no guard against disabling a routed provider. Those questions are undecided.

commit.message:
fix(providers): a custom provider's models must appear the moment it is added

What was broken. Adding a custom provider on the Providers tab produced a
healthy-looking card announcing its models while /v1/models, the Models page
and every Model Config picker held none of them. The only recovery was a
restart -- or, by accident, a second registry mutation.

The mechanism. POST /admin/api/custom-providers called two things that each
went to the upstream. ProviderRuntimeManager.replace() fires a fire-and-forget
sweep of *every* provider's /models, and the route then awaited test_provider,
which fetches /models again. A host registered one second earlier was therefore
asked for its model list twice, concurrently, with the same brand-new key; on
the reported install the sweep's fetch came back PermissionDeniedError. That
failure was only logged (discovery.py swallowed it into a warning), and the
response's `models` array came from the *test*, not from the catalogue -- so
the card could truthfully report 44 models that nothing else in the process
had. A PATCH nine minutes later re-swept and cached them, which is what the
report attributed to a restart that never happened.

The fix.
- replace() takes background_refresh; a registry mutation names the one
  provider it changed and gets ProviderRuntimeManager.refresh_provider_models
  instead: one awaited, provider-scoped discovery with one bounded retry.
- The create/update/key routes report the catalogue they just filled, plus a
  `discovery` block ({ok, model_count, error_type, message}). A failure is no
  longer silent: the response says so and the card renders it red with the
  upstream's reason.
- ProviderDiscoveryFailure carries the reason back to the caller instead of
  dying in a log line.
- cache_enriched_model_infos is now the single cache-and-publish seam, so the
  admin refresh button and background discovery both enrich from models.dev
  before caching. The catalogue no longer depends on which one filled it.
- The custom card's "Test" button is "Refresh models", matching the identical
  call on a static remote card ("Test connection" stays for local ones), and
  updateCustomProviderCard now rewrites the model-count line.

Verification. 15 new tests (route-level end-to-end with only the upstream HTTP
client doubled, provider-level, manager-level, /v1/models and model-admin) plus
2 jsdom tests. Full suite green against the known 15-failure local baseline (8
websearch reading the real ~/.fcc/.env, 6 PowerShell installer, 1 pre-existing
provider-manager catalog-publication test). Browser-driven on a scratch server
with a redirected HOME and a local stub upstream: the stub records exactly one
/models hit per create, the card reads 44 models with no reload, /v1/models
lists both prefixed variants, model-admin reports 44, the pickers offer the
refs, MODEL/MODEL_FALLBACKS round-trip a custom ref, codex-model-catalog.json
is rewritten, and the 403 path renders an error card with zero console errors.

Not done. Part B of the spec (models.dev provider-id field, gateway-style hint,
per-key health readout, onboarding count, disable guard) is undecided and
untouched. No periodic re-discovery timer was added.
